skill.name: bark-notify
skill.description: Send Bark push notifications when a Codex or Claude task finishes, using project, device, status, and summary details.
skill.summary: Send Bark completion alerts for Codex and Claude workflows.
skill.author: caopulan

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally sends Bark notifications to a configured endpoint and reads environment variables for that workflow. Most static Markdown, placeholder, and hidden-path matches are false positives, but task metadata egress and dry-run token exposure remain real risks.

remediation.issue: Notification content can expose workspace metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Add stronger guidance to omit secrets, user data, ticket details, private repository names, and sensitive summaries before sending alerts.

remediation.issue: Dry-run output prints the full Bark URL with the key.
remediation.suggestion: Mask CODEX_BARK_KEY in dry-run output and any future debug logging.

remediation.issue: The Bark key may be stored in shell startup files.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a secret manager or session-scoped environment variable when possible.

remediation.issue: Custom Bark base URLs can receive all notification content.
remediation.suggestion: Document that CODEX_BARK_BASE_URL should use a trusted HTTPS endpoint only.

content.value_statement: AI coding runs can finish while the user is away from the terminal. This skill sends a Bark push alert with project, status, and summary details.
actual_capabilities: Sends Bark push notifications through the day.app API.
Reads CODEX_MACHINE_NAME, CODEX_BARK_KEY, and CODEX_BARK_BASE_URL from the environment.
Includes device, project, status, and summary fields in the alert body.
Resolves project names from AGENTS.md frontmatter or project name lines.
Supports a command-line project override, timeout option, and dry-run mode.
limitations: Requires a valid Bark key and machine name before sending alerts.
Sends task metadata to the configured Bark endpoint.
Does not redact secrets from titles, summaries, or project names.
Cannot guarantee delivery when the network or Bark service fails.

use_cases.title: Notify after long coding runs
use_cases.description: Send a phone alert when a Codex or Claude task completes away from the terminal.

use_cases.title: Track automation outcomes
use_cases.description: Receive status alerts for maintenance tasks, test runs, or documentation updates.

use_cases.title: Monitor shared project work
use_cases.description: Include project names and concise results so reviewers know which task finished.

prompt_templates.title: Basic completion alert
prompt_templates.prompt: Notify me when this run finishes. Use bark-notify with a short title, final status, and brief summary.

prompt_templates.title: Project-aware alert
prompt_templates.scenario: Include project context in the message
prompt_templates.prompt: After completing the requested changes, send a Bark alert that names the project and states the final result in one sentence.

prompt_templates.title: Test result alert
prompt_templates.prompt: When you finish the test run, send a Bark notification with status partial if any checks could not run.

prompt_templates.title: Redacted workflow alert
prompt_templates.prompt: For this repository task, derive the project name from AGENTS.md, redact sensitive details, then send a concise Bark completion alert.

output_examples.input: A user asks Codex to fix a bug and notify them when done.
output_examples.output: The user receives a Bark alert titled Bug fix complete. The body lists device, project, success status, and a short outcome summary.

output_examples.input: A test command fails during a maintenance task.
output_examples.output: The user receives a Bark alert with failed status and a concise summary of the failing check.

output_examples.input: A task completes but one verification step could not run.
output_examples.output: The user receives a Bark alert with partial status and a note explaining the missing verification.

best_practices: Keep notification summaries short and free of secrets.
Use a trusted HTTPS Bark endpoint and rotate the Bark key when needed.
Use dry-run mode only in private terminals because it may show sensitive values.
anti_patterns: Do not include access tokens, customer data, or private incident details in summaries.
Do not send alerts to an untrusted custom base URL.
Do not rely on notifications as the only record of task results.

faq.question: What does this skill send?
faq.answer: It sends a Bark push notification with device name, project name, status, task title, and summary.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it require a Bark account?
faq.answer: It requires a Bark key for the day.app service or a compatible self-hosted endpoint.

faq.question: Can it choose a project name automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper checks AGENTS.md for project name fields, then falls back to the folder name.

faq.question: Does it protect secrets automatically?
faq.answer: No. Users and agents must avoid putting secrets or sensitive data in notification text.

faq.question: Can I test it without sending a notification?
faq.answer: Yes. Dry-run mode prints the request details, but it can show sensitive values.
